Although you can’t remove previous versions of a crate, you can prevent any future projects from adding them as a new dependency. This is useful when a crate version is broken for one reason or another. In such situations, Cargo supports yanking a crate version.
a version prevents new projects from depending on that version while allowing all existing projects that depend on it to continue. Essentially, a yank means that all projects with a
will not break, and any future
files generated will not use the yanked version.
To yank a version of a crate, in the directory of the crate that you’ve previously published, run
and specify which version you want to yank. For example, if we’ve published a crate named
version 1.0.1 and we want to yank it, then we’d run the following in the project directory for

blocks.code:
$ cargo yank --vers 1.0.1
    Updating crates.io index
        Yank guessing_game@1.0.1

text.v: to the command, you can also undo a yank and allow projects to start depending on a version again:

blocks.code:
